I'll just add to it: even before @nanbeige , Bytedance showed that looped transformer work in their ouro paper

https://t.co/jmQmT593Eb

an interesting conclusion from their experiment was that a looped model was outperforming models roughly 2.5x their size. 

it would be tempting to think that looping compresses ~2-3x more intelligence per parameter, but subsequent ablations and papers found that the knowledge/intelligence per parameter remains same (whatever that parameter budget can encode) but it's looping -- latent thinking that brings out more out of model, just like Reasoning which is an emergent property for a model, and RLVR teaches model to use it's world knowledge better, looped transformer (trained entirely via pre training) not only "learns" but also learns to "think" and how to think in pretraining stage,

I am still not convinced about this risk with respect to the looped transformer architecture modification (i.e. how looped transformers "hide" reasoning in a significant way). 

The argument is that looped transformers might be hiding reasoning because they do more internal computation (loops). 

But then, we can say the same thing about GPT 5.6 Luna and GPT 5.6 Sol. The latter is likely bigger and has more layers, but I haven't heard anyone being concerned about the fact that Sol hides its reasoning (even though larger models typically require fewer tokens to solve a given task)

@goldstein_aa Is it an interesting change? Yes! 
Is it a "major change"? Hm, I don't know.

I think the hybrid attention methods are more "major".

But yeah, at least something new in any case ☺️
@technotweet How why would this happen? You can say the same thing that since GPT 5.6 Sol has more layers than GPT 5.6 Luna, it has more "Neuralese" replacing readable CoT?

The YT version of this:
https://t.co/VRL5dPMTk5
@BugLukas @mkovarski Haven't seen this, and this is super cool and informative. But it could also look similar if you overlay GPT 5.4 and GPT 5.6
@prdeepakbabu yeah, this paper is basically the universal transformer with more residual connections to the input
@crystalwizard yeah exactly
@KentaGold we don't, which is why I mentioned both 😆
@singularitywen maybe the best way to answer it is: it doesn't change how reasoning works in current models, it just uses more internal compute (analogous to adding more layers)

@mattturck I don't think it's related to RSI.

But given RAM prices, I think this is not a bad idea. You still grow the KV cache but not as much compared to increasing the overall size of the model if you use the routing.
@schwarzjn_ From a safety perspective, I don't think it makes a difference whether you add more layers or reuse the existing layers?

@aaryan_kakad Yeah, it's a different mechanism of using more compute. Either via more iterations in the transformer loop or by using more CoT tokens.
I wouldn't say more or less uncertain though. If a router is used, that one can mess up as well.
@spolen23 Run a version of the model with and without looping on reasoning tasks that it can solve well, then see if the looped variant uses fewer tokens.
@Blum_OG haha yes

@bytecrafter_1 Yeah, I added a uv.lock to help a little. But pinning too much can also cause issues. I.e., there are people who can't run the a specific version (due to CUDA compatibility) with specific drivers and so on. The default works for most people but not everyone, yes.
